whole_expression_publication_assessment.Semen_basis: The complete old Latin antiphon is directly verified in the registered 1888 Pustet source with its affirmative publication-date basis and exact public-domain Latin carrier. Later OLM pointing introduces no new substantive expression.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.Lasance_Latin_basis: The repository rights inventory, pinned in each affected case, separately identifies the latin-missale-romanum layer as the old Tridentine Latin through Benedict XV, public domain by its own age. whole_expression_publication_assessment.whole_expression_reasoning: Each displayed verse is one complete old source unit, with all words in the original order. None is assembled from scattered old fragments or reconstructed from a Bible citation. The only recorded changes are chant-mark removal, accent/ligature and line-wrap normalization, or punctuation. Considered as a whole, none adds a new developed clause, substantive alteration or expressive arrangement. The publication basis is the independent old whole expression; OLM establishes exact appointment and comparison only.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.strongest_adverse_argument: A modern liturgical book may contain protected editing or arrangement, and the presence of old words in a later book does not clear that book or its selection as a whole. The mixed late Lasance scan likewise cannot be treated as entirely public domain. English permission does not automatically license Latin.
whole_expression_publication_assessment.response: The finite body for each recipient is the exact complete historical verse, not the surrounding modern book, rubrics or selection. Source layers, bounds and recipient appointments are separately identified. No substantive modern recasting is present in any of these seven bodies. Whole-book scans and surrounding apparatus remain outside publication. This is a bounded internal project assessment rather than rightsholder permission or a court ruling.
